text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The majority of Poles are planning to take part in the constitutional referendum scheduled for May 25. Over 50 percent of the prospective voters are ready to vote in favour of the parliamentary draft, a recent survey by the PBS polling agency said.

- The rightist Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) will mail four million leaflets calling on the voters to vote against the parliamentary constitutional draft in the referendum, ROP said.
- Poland will join the EU educational development programme in autumn this year. Polish students will be allowed to participate in various exchange programmes between European universities.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's textile industry does not have to fear integration with the EU as it has been improving product quality and cutting costs for years, Poland's European Integration Committee secretary Danuta Huebner said.

- Solidarity trade union at the Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecoms monopolist has demanded that only a nine percent share stake in the company should be sold in a public offer and the obtained funds should go into the company's modernisation rather than to the state treasury.
- The clients of the PTK Centertel analogue mobile phone firm will be able to use their phones in Finland thanks to a roaming agreement signed with the Finnish Tele mobile phone firm.
- Fiat Auto Poland (FAP) produced 307,000 cars last year and its sales reached 327,000 cars. It exported 162,000 vehicles. The company netted 311 million zlotys.
- The state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) food economy bank will launch the Krajowa Korporacja Leasingowa (KKL) leasing fund in mid-May. KKL's founding capital is 600,000 zlotys.

- The Energo-Asekuracja insurance firm is planning to double its share capital this year. Shares from the new issues will be taken up by current shareholders and a U.S. investor. The company's present share capital is 7.5 million zlotys.

- The following banks launched electronic home banking services in the last few months: BGZ, Bank Zachodni, the Bank Wschodnio Europejski (BWE), Bank Incjatyw Spoleczno- Ekonomicznych (BISE) and Rabo-BRP Bank Polska.
- Poland's finance ministry has confirmed its decision to collect tax on profit uncollected in dividend by the shareholders in limited liability companies, the ministry said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Poland's way to th EU will be both long and difficult, the EU ambassador to Poland Rolf Timans said. Poles should have solid information on the opportunities and difficulties related to the EU integration, Timans said.
- The European Bank of Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) will buy a part of the new share issue of Kredyt Bank (KB) to preserve its stake in the bank at the 7.8 percent level, EBRD said.
- Around 75.7 percent of adult Poles buy beer and lager sales are growing at the fastest rate, a recent survey by the Indicator market research agency said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Nestle food processing concern will inject the remaining part of $30 million earmarked for development of the Winiary food concentrate plant by the end of July, Winiary's president Karol Madrowski said.
ZYCIE
- Poland's 1996 paper output was worth 4.2 billion zlotys, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said. Exports accounted for 1.4 billion zlotys and imports for 3.2 billion zlotys.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
